lead: Clearwater sits on Tampa Bay with a barrier-island beach out front. Helene's storm surge in 2024 broke records there, and older homes and mobile homes add everyday risks.
risk: storm surge, aging plumbing and mobile home leaks
risk_short: storm surge, old pipes, mobile homes
why: Hurricane Helene passed far offshore in September 2024, but it still pushed about 6.5 feet of surge onto Clearwater Beach. Gulf water ran through the streets of the barrier island and into ground-floor homes, condos and hotels. Many residents said it was the first time their homes had ever flooded. Two weeks later, Milton brought wind and heavy rain across the county.

Away from the beach, age is the main issue. About 56% of Clearwater homes were built before 1980, many with cast-iron drains and original supply lines. About 5% of homes are mobile or manufactured homes, where leaks under the floor can rot the subfloor unseen. In this humid climate, wet drywall and carpet grow mold fast if they are not dried.
image_alt: Beachfront building battered by storm waves and debris
image_caption: Helene's surge pushed Gulf water through Clearwater Beach streets in 2024.
problems: Clearwater Beach, Island Estates, Sand Key
Pre-1980 homes in Harbor Oaks, Morningside
tips: Know your evacuation zone; surge is the deadliest part of a storm.
Have pre-1980 cast-iron drains scoped with a camera.
Check under a mobile home for drips and soft floors twice a year.
Photograph each room before hurricane season for your claim.
areas: Calls come from Clearwater Beach, Island Estates, Sand Key, Downtown, Harbor Oaks, Countryside, Morningside and Glenwood, plus Dunedin, Largo and Safety Harbor.

faq.q: Does my Clearwater home policy cover storm surge?
faq.a: No. Surge and rising water need a flood policy from the NFIP or a private insurer. Your home policy may cover wind damage and rain that gets in through a damaged roof, usually with a separate hurricane deductible.
